newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares set high, profit-taking expected.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares set high, profit-taking expected.

text.p: Polish shares jumped in surging turnover for the second consecutive session on Wednesday, setting a 33-month high, but analysts saw them falling on profit-taking on Thursday.
The main market's WIG index rose 2.1 percent, to 15,087.9, and turnover rose 30.9 percent to 200.5 million zlotys ($67 million) on both markets as 73 issues rose, five fell and six were flat.

"One can expect the market to fall, taking into account the strong selling after price fixing....Usually such intense growth is followed by a fall," said Stanislaw Kutkowski, a trader at Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) brokerage.

Analysts were divided on the market's subsequent direction. Some said institutional buying might help set more highs while others saw stabilisation because of approaching new issues, the threat of an interest rate rise as early as mid-month and companies' likely unspectacular December earnings.

Analysts said Wednesday's news of food-price growth of 0.3 percent in December 21-31 was unlikely to move the market in the next few sessions, but they said investors still feared a rate raise at mid-month, as the central bank says is possible.
Analysts could not explain construction firm Mostostal Warszawa's 9.6-percent rise, its second consecutive jump by more than 9.5 percent, and construction company Budimex's surge of 9.9 percent.
They said paintmaker Polifarb Wroclaw, which rose 9.3 percent, was still benefiting from the news it planned to merge with Polifarb Cieszyn.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 1.4 percent in 16.5-million-zloty ($5.7 million) trade in the regular session and were flat in 13.9-million-zloty ($4.8 million) continuous trade.
